title: Heat Transfer
description: Heat Transfer covers conduction, convection, radiation, phase change, and heat exchangers, with synthesis topics on thermal systems modeling and mass-transfer analogies for engineering thermal design.

topics.title: Modes of Heat Transfer Overview
topics.description: This opening topic frames heat transfer as energy moving because of temperature differences. Students learn when conduction, convection, radiation, and combined modes dominate.

children.title: Thermal energy and temperature gradients
children.description: Students learn the physical driver for heat transfer and why temperature fields are central to analysis.

children.title: Conduction
children.description: Conduction explains heat flow through solids and stationary media by molecular and lattice interactions.

children.title: Convection
children.description: Convection combines heat diffusion at a surface with fluid motion near that surface.

children.title: Radiation
children.description: Radiation transfers energy by electromagnetic emission and can matter even through vacuum.

topics.title: Conduction (1D Steady-State)
topics.description: Steady one-dimensional conduction is the first quantitative model students use to connect geometry, material properties, and temperature difference to heat flow.

children.title: Fourier's law in one dimension
children.description: Fourier's law turns a temperature gradient into heat flux.

children.title: Thermal resistance networks
children.description: Resistance networks make conduction problems look like circuit problems, which is useful for layered systems.

children.title: Contact resistance
children.description: Real interfaces are imperfect, so contact resistance can dominate practical assemblies.

children.title: Heat generation
children.description: Internal generation appears in electronics, nuclear fuel, batteries, and biological or chemical systems.

topics.title: Multi-Dimensional Conduction
topics.description: Many real objects do not conduct heat in only one direction. This topic expands conduction analysis to fins, shape factors, and spatial temperature fields.

children.title: Two- and three-dimensional temperature fields
children.description: Students learn when one-dimensional assumptions break down.

children.title: Extended surfaces and fins
children.description: Fins increase heat transfer area but introduce temperature variation along the fin.

children.title: Shape factors
children.description: Shape factors provide practical estimates for conduction through complex geometries.

children.title: Numerical conduction preview
children.description: Students see why numerical methods become necessary for complex geometry and mixed boundary conditions.

topics.title: Transient Conduction
topics.description: Transient conduction studies how temperature changes with time during heating, cooling, quenching, start-up, or thermal cycling.

children.title: Lumped capacitance method
children.description: Lumped analysis is the simplest time-dependent thermal model when internal temperature gradients are small.

children.title: One-term and chart solutions
children.description: Approximate transient solutions help analyze slabs, cylinders, and spheres when internal gradients matter.

children.title: Semi-infinite solids
children.description: Short-time heating and cooling often behave like heat transfer into a semi-infinite medium.

children.title: Thermal cycling and response
children.description: Students learn to interpret transient response for design reliability and control.

topics.title: Convection Fundamentals
topics.description: Convection depends on both fluid mechanics and thermal diffusion. Students learn how boundary layers, dimensionless numbers, and correlations organize the complexity.

children.title: Boundary layers
children.description: Boundary layers explain why surface heat transfer is controlled by near-wall velocity and temperature gradients.

children.title: Dimensionless groups
children.description: Dimensionless numbers summarize competing effects and guide correlation use.

children.title: Heat transfer coefficients
children.description: The heat transfer coefficient packages complex convection physics into a practical design parameter.

children.title: Analogy to momentum transfer
children.description: Momentum and heat transfer share boundary-layer structure, enabling useful engineering analogies.

topics.title: Forced Convection
topics.description: Forced convection occurs when fans, pumps, wind, or other imposed flows move fluid over or through heated surfaces.

children.title: External forced convection
children.description: External-flow correlations predict heat transfer from plates, cylinders, spheres, and bodies in flow.

children.title: Internal forced convection
children.description: Internal-flow models support pipe, duct, cooling channel, and heat-exchanger design.

children.title: Constant wall temperature and heat flux
Laminar and turbulent correlations
children.description: Students learn to choose correlations based on geometry, flow regime, and boundary conditions.

children.title: Pressure drop and pumping power
children.description: Heat transfer gains often come with flow-resistance costs.

topics.title: Natural Convection
topics.description: Natural convection is driven by buoyancy, making it central to passive cooling, building heat loss, environmental flows, and electronics enclosures.

children.title: Buoyancy-driven flow
children.description: Students learn how density differences create motion without a fan or pump.

children.title: Natural convection dimensionless groups
children.description: Special dimensionless numbers capture buoyancy and diffusion effects.

children.title: External natural convection
children.description: Common surface geometries have useful natural-convection correlations.

children.title: Enclosures and mixed convection
children.description: Real systems often combine buoyancy with confinement or forced flow.

topics.title: Boiling and Condensation
topics.description: Phase-change heat transfer can move large heat rates with small temperature differences, but it also introduces regimes, limits, and safety concerns.

children.title: Boiling regimes
children.description: Students learn how boiling behavior changes from isolated bubbles to crisis conditions.

children.title: Boiling curves and critical heat flux
children.description: The boiling curve is essential for understanding performance and failure limits.

children.title: Condensation modes
children.description: Condensation can occur as a film or droplets, with very different heat-transfer performance.

children.title: Phase-change applications
children.description: Students connect phase change to real thermal systems and equipment.

topics.title: Heat Exchangers
topics.description: Heat exchangers are a major engineering application where conduction and convection are combined into practical equipment for energy transfer.

children.title: Heat-exchanger types
children.description: Students learn the main configurations and when each is useful.

children.title: Log mean temperature difference method
children.description: LMTD analysis converts changing temperature differences into a design calculation.

children.title: Effectiveness-NTU method
children.description: Effectiveness-NTU is useful when outlet temperatures are unknown or exchanger sizing is being compared.

children.title: Design constraints
children.description: Real exchanger design balances heat transfer, pressure drop, fouling, cost, and maintainability.

topics.title: Radiation Heat Transfer
topics.description: Radiation heat transfer governs high-temperature systems, furnaces, solar energy, spacecraft thermal control, and surface-to-surface exchange.

children.title: Blackbody radiation
children.description: Blackbody laws provide the ideal reference for thermal emission.

children.title: Real surfaces
children.description: Real materials emit, absorb, reflect, and transmit radiation in wavelength- and direction-dependent ways.

children.title: View factors
children.description: Geometry controls how much radiation leaving one surface reaches another.

children.title: Radiation exchange networks
children.description: Network methods make enclosure radiation calculations manageable.

topics.title: Thermal Systems, Properties, and Numerical Modeling
topics.description: This added synthesis topic connects heat transfer theory to design practice, material data, and computational modeling.

children.title: Thermophysical properties
children.description: Accurate properties are necessary for credible heat-transfer calculations.

children.title: Thermal resistance and capacitance models
children.description: Simple system-level models help estimate temperatures before detailed simulation.

children.title: Numerical methods
children.description: Numerical modeling handles geometries, property variation, and coupled boundary conditions that closed-form methods cannot.

children.title: Design and validation workflow
children.description: Students learn to connect calculations, simulations, measurements, and engineering decisions.

topics.title: Mass Transfer Analogies and Coupled Transport
topics.description: This added topic introduces mass-transfer parallels and coupled heat/mass problems, reflecting the chemical engineering and graduate transport context around the course.

children.title: Diffusion fundamentals
children.description: Diffusion provides the mass-transfer counterpart to conduction.

children.title: Convective mass transfer
children.description: Convective mass transfer mirrors convective heat transfer through boundary layers and coefficients.

children.title: Simultaneous heat and mass transfer
children.description: Many real systems transfer heat and mass at the same time.

children.title: Applications and limits
children.description: Students learn where analogies are useful and where phase change, reactions, or property variation complicate them.
